title: Social Conversations
tagline: Find the words for friendly everyday moments.
description: Build confidence in everyday conversations, from meeting new people and sharing interests to making plans, showing care, and clearing up small misunderstandings.

chapters.title: A Friendly First Hello
chapters.description: Introduce yourself, welcome someone, and begin a relaxed conversation.

sentences.text: Hi, I'm new to this neighborhood.
sentences.hint: Explain that you recently moved to the area.

sentences.text: Is this your first time at the club?
sentences.hint: Ask whether someone has visited the group before.

sentences.text: It's nice to meet someone who lives nearby.
sentences.hint: Show pleasure at meeting a local person.

sentences.text: What do you like to do on weekends?
sentences.hint: Ask about someone's free-time activities.

sentences.text: I work at a small shop near the station.
sentences.hint: Describe your job and its location.

sentences.text: How do you know the host?
sentences.hint: Ask about someone's connection to the party organizer.

sentences.text: Please call me by my first name.
sentences.hint: Invite someone to use a less formal name.

sentences.text: There's a free seat next to me.
sentences.hint: Let someone know they can sit beside you.

sentences.text: Would you like to join our conversation?
sentences.hint: Invite another person into the discussion.

sentences.text: I'm glad we finally had a chance to talk.
sentences.hint: Say that you enjoyed getting to know someone.

chapters.title: Little Everyday Chats
chapters.description: Keep a conversation going with simple questions and everyday observations.

sentences.text: Did you have a good morning?
sentences.hint: Ask how the first part of someone's day went.

sentences.text: The park looks lovely in the sunshine.
sentences.hint: Comment on a pleasant outdoor scene.

sentences.text: My bus was late, so I walked here.
sentences.hint: Explain why you came on foot.

sentences.text: That jacket is a really nice color.
sentences.hint: Give a simple compliment about someone's clothes.

sentences.text: Have you tried the new bakery?
sentences.hint: Ask whether someone has bought food from a recently opened shop.

sentences.text: I usually stop here for coffee after work.
sentences.hint: Describe a regular visit at the end of your working day.

sentences.text: Was the market busy today?
sentences.hint: Ask whether there were many shoppers.

sentences.text: Your dog seems very friendly.
sentences.hint: Make a warm comment about someone's pet.

sentences.text: It's getting cold outside, isn't it?
sentences.hint: Invite agreement about a change in the weather.

sentences.text: I hope the rain stops before your walk home.
sentences.hint: Wish someone better weather for their journey.

chapters.title: What We Enjoy
chapters.description: Share your tastes and discover interests you have in common.

sentences.text: I'd rather watch a comedy tonight.
sentences.hint: Choose a funny film over other kinds.

sentences.text: Do you prefer cooking at home or eating out?
sentences.hint: Ask which kind of meal experience someone likes more.

sentences.text: I love music, but I can't play an instrument.
sentences.hint: Describe an interest without claiming a musical skill.

sentences.text: Swimming helps me relax after a busy day.
sentences.hint: Explain how a water activity makes you feel calmer.

sentences.text: What kind of books do you usually read?
sentences.hint: Find out about someone's reading tastes.

sentences.text: I'm not very interested in watching sports.
sentences.hint: Politely say that sports programs are not your favorite.

sentences.text: This soup is a little too spicy for me.
sentences.hint: Explain that a dish has more heat than you enjoy.

sentences.text: We both enjoy taking photos of nature.
sentences.hint: Point out a shared outdoor hobby.

sentences.text: Could you recommend an easy board game?
sentences.hint: Ask for a suggestion that is simple to learn.

sentences.text: I'd like to try dancing, even though I'm shy.
sentences.hint: Show interest in a new activity despite feeling nervous.

chapters.title: You're Invited
chapters.description: Offer invitations, accept warmly, and say no without sounding unfriendly.

sentences.text: Would you like to come over for dinner on Friday?
sentences.hint: Invite someone to an evening meal at your home.

sentences.text: We're having a picnic, and you're welcome to come.
sentences.hint: Include someone in an outdoor meal.

sentences.text: Thank you for asking, but I already have plans.
sentences.hint: Decline politely because you are not free.

sentences.text: I'd love to go to the concert with you.
sentences.hint: Accept an invitation to hear live music.

sentences.text: Is it all right if I bring a friend?
sentences.hint: Check whether another guest can join you.

sentences.text: You don't need to bring any food.
sentences.hint: Tell a guest that the meal is already covered.

sentences.text: Saturday is difficult for me, but Sunday is fine.
sentences.hint: Offer a different day when you are available.

sentences.text: Can I let you know tomorrow morning?
sentences.hint: Ask for more time before giving an answer.

sentences.text: Let's invite the neighbors to our barbecue.
sentences.hint: Suggest including the people who live nearby.

sentences.text: Thank you for inviting me to such a lovely evening.
sentences.hint: Show appreciation after an enjoyable visit.

chapters.title: How We Feel
chapters.description: Talk about emotions and respond with interest and care.

sentences.text: I'm excited about my first painting lesson.
sentences.hint: Share a happy feeling about starting a creative class.

sentences.text: You seem quiet today; is everything okay?
sentences.hint: Gently check on someone who is not talking much.

sentences.text: I've had a long day, and I need some rest.
sentences.hint: Explain that you feel tired and want a break.

sentences.text: I'm sorry your trip didn't go well.
sentences.hint: Show sympathy after a disappointing journey.

sentences.text: Talking to you always makes me feel better.
sentences.hint: Explain that a friend's company improves your mood.

sentences.text: Are you nervous about meeting the group?
sentences.hint: Ask whether a social event is causing worry.

sentences.text: I'm proud of myself for trying something new.
sentences.hint: Share satisfaction about stepping outside your usual routine.

sentences.text: You don't have to talk about it right now.
sentences.hint: Give someone space to share their feelings later.

sentences.text: I'm so relieved to hear that you're feeling better!
sentences.hint: Express happiness that someone's health has improved.

sentences.text: Would a short walk help you feel less worried?
sentences.hint: Suggest gentle exercise as a way to relax.

chapters.title: Let's Make a Plan
chapters.description: Agree on times, places, and simple changes to shared plans.

sentences.text: Shall we meet outside the cinema at six?
sentences.hint: Suggest a meeting point and an evening time.

sentences.text: The earlier train gives us more time at the beach.
sentences.hint: Explain the benefit of leaving sooner.

sentences.text: Which day works best for everyone?
sentences.hint: Ask the group to choose a convenient date.

sentences.text: I'll book a table once we choose a restaurant.
sentences.hint: Offer to arrange seats after the group makes a decision.

sentences.text: Could we start a little later than usual?
sentences.hint: Request a small change to the normal starting time.

sentences.text: If it rains, we can have lunch at my place.
sentences.hint: Offer an indoor option for bad weather.

sentences.text: Let's check the opening times before we leave.
sentences.hint: Suggest confirming when a place is open.

sentences.text: I'm running ten minutes late, but I'm on my way.
sentences.hint: Tell someone about a short delay while you are traveling.

sentences.text: Do we have enough time for a quick coffee?
sentences.hint: Check whether a brief café stop fits the schedule.

sentences.text: Please send me a message if the plan changes.
sentences.hint: Ask to be told about any new arrangements.

chapters.title: Small Acts of Kindness
chapters.description: Ask for favors, offer practical help, and respect other people's time.

sentences.text: Could you hold the door while I carry these bags?
sentences.hint: Request a little help with a heavy load.

sentences.text: I can water your plants while you're away.
sentences.hint: Offer to care for something during a friend's trip.

sentences.text: Would you mind taking a photo of us?
sentences.hint: Politely ask someone to use the camera for your group.

sentences.text: You made moving the sofa much easier.
sentences.hint: Show appreciation for assistance with furniture.

sentences.text: You can borrow my umbrella until tomorrow.
sentences.hint: Offer temporary use of something that keeps the rain off.

sentences.text: Is there anything I can do to help with dinner?
sentences.hint: Offer assistance while a meal is being prepared.

sentences.text: I can't stay long, but I can help you tidy up.
sentences.hint: Offer a little help before you need to leave.

sentences.text: Please don't worry about returning the book today.
sentences.hint: Tell someone there is no hurry to give something back.

sentences.text: Let me know if the music is too loud.
sentences.hint: Invite someone to speak up about the noise.

sentences.text: I'd like to help, but I need a quiet evening alone.
sentences.hint: Kindly explain that you need personal time instead.

chapters.title: Different Ideas, Still Friends
chapters.description: Express another opinion gently and find choices that suit both people.

sentences.text: I see what you mean, but I enjoyed the ending.
sentences.hint: Respect another view while giving your own reaction to a story.

sentences.text: That café is nice, although it's a bit noisy.
sentences.hint: Mention a drawback without rejecting a place completely.

sentences.text: Are you sure that route is the shortest?
sentences.hint: Gently question someone's choice of directions.

sentences.text: I'd prefer somewhere cheaper for lunch.
sentences.hint: Politely suggest spending less on a meal.

sentences.text: Maybe we have different tastes in music.
sentences.hint: Explain a disagreement as a difference in personal preference.

sentences.text: Could we choose a film that we both want to see?
sentences.hint: Ask for an entertainment choice everyone can enjoy.

sentences.text: I don't think the weather is warm enough for swimming.
sentences.hint: Give a reason for not wanting to get in the water.

sentences.text: Let's take turns choosing where we go.
sentences.hint: Suggest sharing decisions fairly over time.

sentences.text: You might be right about leaving before the traffic gets bad.
sentences.hint: Accept that another person's travel advice may be sensible.

sentences.text: We don't have to agree on everything to have fun together.
sentences.hint: Reassure a friend that different opinions are okay.

chapters.title: Keeping Friendship Close
chapters.description: Stay connected, celebrate good news, and make room for each other.

sentences.text: It's been a while since we last had lunch together.
sentences.hint: Mention that you have not shared a meal recently.

sentences.text: How did your driving test go?
sentences.hint: Follow up on an important event in a friend's life.

sentences.text: I saw a funny postcard and thought of you.
sentences.hint: Explain that a small discovery reminded you of a friend.

sentences.text: I'm so happy you've found a place of your own!
sentences.hint: Celebrate someone's move into their own home.

sentences.text: Can we catch up on the phone this weekend?
sentences.hint: Suggest a call to share recent news.

sentences.text: I miss our evening walks by the river.
sentences.hint: Say that you wish a shared routine could happen again.

sentences.text: There's no rush to reply if you're busy.
sentences.hint: Remove pressure to answer your message immediately.

sentences.text: You've always been a good listener.
sentences.hint: Appreciate a friend's attention and understanding.

sentences.text: Let's make more time for each other next month.
sentences.hint: Suggest seeing a friend more often in the near future.

sentences.text: Even a short visit would be lovely.
sentences.hint: Show that you would appreciate a little time together.

chapters.title: Clearing Things Up
chapters.description: Check what someone means, explain mistakes, and repair small misunderstandings.

sentences.text: Sorry, I thought we were meeting at the other entrance.
sentences.hint: Explain a mistake about the agreed meeting point.

sentences.text: Did you mean this Thursday or next Thursday?
sentences.hint: Check which week a person is talking about.

sentences.text: I didn't mean to sound rude on the phone.
sentences.hint: Explain that an unfriendly tone was not intentional.

sentences.text: Could you explain what you meant by that message?
sentences.hint: Ask for a clearer explanation of a written comment.

sentences.text: I wasn't ignoring you; my phone was on silent.
sentences.hint: Explain why you did not notice someone's call.

sentences.text: I'm glad you told me how you felt about the joke.
sentences.hint: Appreciate someone's honesty about a comment that upset them.

sentences.text: I should have asked before I shared your photo.
sentences.hint: Admit that you needed permission for something you did.

sentences.text: Let's talk about this when we both feel calmer.
sentences.hint: Suggest waiting until a difficult conversation will be easier.

sentences.text: I'm glad we understand each other better now.
sentences.hint: Express relief after resolving some confusion.

sentences.text: Can we start again and make a new plan?
sentences.hint: Invite a fresh attempt after an arrangement went wrong.
